title: Hybrid self-suspension models in real-time embedded systems

extraction.paper_name: Hybrid Self-Suspension Models in Real-Time Embedded Systems
extraction.paper_description: The paper introduces hybrid self-suspension task models (Pattern-oblivious and Pattern-clairvoyant) to bridge the gap between flexible but pessimistic dynamic models and restrictive but accurate segmented models. It provides schedulability analysis using Demand Bound Functions (DBF) under Fixed-Relative-Deadline (FRD) scheduling.

formal_description.statement: A hybrid self-suspending task tau_i is defined by (T_i, D_i, C_i, S_i, m_i), where C_i is the total WCET, S_i is the total maximum suspension time, and m_i is the maximum number of suspension intervals.

variables.D_i: Relative deadline (D_i = T_i for implicit deadlines)
variables.C_i: Worst-case execution time (sum of computation segments)
variables.S_i: Maximum self-suspension time (sum of suspension intervals)

formal_description.conclusion: Defines the basic parameters for hybrid self-suspension tasks.

informal_sketch.intuition: A task is a sequence of execution segments separated by gaps where the task waits (suspends). We know how many gaps there are (m_i) and the total time spent executing (C_i) and waiting (S_i).
steps: Initialize task with period T_i and deadline D_i
Set total execution budget C_i
Set total suspension budget S_i
Define structure with m_i suspension points
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
class HybridTask:
    def __init__(self, T_i, C_i, S_i, m_i):
        self.T_i = T_i
        self.D_i = T_i
        self.C_i = C_i
        self.S_i = S_i
        self.m_i = m_i
key_insights: Hybrid models use m_i to reduce pessimism compared to dynamic models which ignore the number of suspensions.

formal_description.statement: The Pattern-Oblivious Individual Upper Bounds (IUB) model assumes C_i_j <= C_max_i_j for j in {1, ..., m_i+1} and S_i_j <= S_max_i_j for j in {1, ..., m_i}.

variables.C_i_j: Execution time of the j-th segment
variables.C_max_i_j: Upper bound on the j-th execution segment
variables.S_max_i_j: Upper bound on the j-th suspension interval

formal_description.conclusion: Defines a model where individual segment bounds are known but the specific path is not.

informal_sketch.intuition: We don't know exactly which path the task takes, but we have a 'worst-case' limit for every single piece of the task's execution and suspension.
steps: Identify maximum possible execution for each segment j
Identify maximum possible suspension for each interval j
Ensure the sum of these parts covers the global worst-case C_i and S_i
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def define_IUB_model(task, C_max_list, S_max_list):
    task.C_max_segments = C_max_list
    task.S_max_intervals = S_max_list
    return task
key_insights: This is more restrictive than the dynamic model but more flexible than the segmented model.

formal_description.statement: The Pattern-Oblivious Multiple Paths (MP) model describes task tau_i as a set of p triples: {(C_1_i_1, S_1_i, C_1_i_2), ..., (C_p_i_1, S_p_i, C_p_i_2)} for m_i = 1.

variables.C_j_i_1: WCET of segment 1 in path j
variables.C_j_i_2: WCET of segment 2 in path j

assumptions: The specific path j is unknown at job arrival time
formal_description.conclusion: Defines a model where the task follows one of several known discrete patterns.

informal_sketch.intuition: The task has a finite set of 'blueprints' (paths). We know all the blueprints, but we don't know which one the task will pick when it starts.
steps: List all possible (C1, S, C2) combinations
Treat the task as a collection of these potential behaviors
key_insights: Captures control flow branches where different paths have different execution/suspension characteristics.

formal_description.statement: A set of jobs J can meet deadlines under EDF if and only if for all intervals [a_i, d_k], the sum of WCETs of jobs arriving and ending within the interval is <= d_k - a_i.

variables.C_j: Worst-case execution time of job j

formal_description.conclusion: Provides the fundamental condition for EDF schedulability.

informal_sketch.intuition: The processor cannot do more work than the time available. If we look at any time window, the total work due in that window must be less than the window's length.
steps: Pick any two time points a_i and d_k
Sum up the execution times of all jobs that must start after a_i and finish before d_k
Check if sum <= d_k - a_i
key_insights: This is the basis for the Demand Bound Function (DBF) analysis.

formal_description.statement: dbf_FRD_i(t, D_i_1) = max(dbf_1_i(t, D_i_1), dbf_2_i(t, D_i_1))

variables.dbf_1_i: Demand when segment 1 is released at t=0
variables.dbf_2_i: Demand when segment 2 is released at t=0

formal_description.conclusion: Calculates the maximum demand of a segmented task under FRD.

informal_sketch.intuition: To find the worst-case demand, we check two scenarios: one where the first part of the task starts right at the beginning of our observation window, and one where the second part starts there.
steps: Calculate demand pattern starting with C_i_1
Calculate demand pattern starting with C_i_2
The true DBF is the maximum of these two at any time t
key_insights: The worst-case alignment for a self-suspending task isn't always the arrival of the first segment.

formal_description.statement: dbf_I_i(t, D_i_1) = max(dbf_I_1_i(t, D_i_1), dbf_I_2_i(t, D_i_1)) where dbf_I_1_i uses C_max_i_1 and dbf_I_2_i uses C_max_i_2.

variables.dbf_I_1_i: Demand for IUB model starting with segment 1
variables.dbf_I_2_i: Demand for IUB model starting with segment 2

formal_description.conclusion: Provides the DBF for the IUB hybrid model.

informal_sketch.intuition: Similar to the segmented model, but we use the individual upper bounds for each segment to ensure we cover the worst case of any possible internal execution pattern.
steps: Use C_max_i_1 to calculate demand when segment 1 starts at 0
Use C_max_i_2 to calculate demand when segment 2 starts at 0
Take the maximum
key_insights: Uses individual segment bounds to tighten the demand compared to just using total C_i.

formal_description.statement: dbf_MP_i(t, D_i_1) = max(dbf_MP_1_i(t, D_i_1), max_j_in_1_to_p(dbf_MP_2_i_j(t, D_i_1)))

variables.dbf_MP_1_i: Demand starting with segment 1 (path independent for D_i_1)
variables.dbf_MP_2_i_j: Demand starting with segment 2 of path j

formal_description.conclusion: Provides the DBF for the Multiple Paths hybrid model.

informal_sketch.intuition: Since we don't know the path, we must assume the worst-case path for every possible alignment. We check the demand if segment 1 starts at 0, and then check every possible path's segment 2 starting at 0.
steps: Calculate demand for segment 1 starting at 0 (uses global C_max_i)
For each path j, calculate demand if its segment 2 starts at 0
The result is the maximum over all these scenarios
key_insights: Even if paths are known, the lack of runtime identification requires taking the maximum over all path-specific DBFs.

variables.dbf_clair_2_i_j: Demand starting with segment 2 of path j

formal_description.conclusion: Provides the DBF for the Pattern-Clairvoyant hybrid model.

informal_sketch.intuition: In the clairvoyant model, we know the path at arrival. This allows us to assign different deadlines to different paths, making the demand calculation more specific and less pessimistic.
steps: Define path-specific deadlines D_j_i_1
Calculate demand for segment 1 starting at 0 using path-specific deadlines
Calculate demand for segment 2 starting at 0 for each path
Take the maximum
key_insights: Clairvoyance allows path-specific deadline assignments, which significantly reduces the DBF compared to oblivious models.

formal_description.statement: An FRD schedule is feasible if and only if sum_{tau_i in T} dbf_FRD_i(t, D_i_1) <= t for all t >= 0.

variables.dbf_FRD_i: Demand bound function for task i

formal_description.conclusion: The necessary and sufficient condition for schedulability under FRD.

informal_sketch.intuition: If the total demand from all tasks in any time interval is never more than the time available, no task will ever miss a deadline.
steps: For every possible time interval length t
Sum the DBFs of all tasks
Verify the sum is <= t
key_insights: Converts the complex scheduling problem into a set of static demand checks.

formal_description.statement: An FRD schedule under a deadline assignment policy A is feasible if sum_{tau_i in T} dbf_A_i(t, D_i_1) <= t for all t >= 0, where dbf_A_i is the DBF corresponding to the hybrid model (IUB, MP, or Clairvoyant).
formal_description.conclusion: Generalizes the FRD schedulability test to all proposed hybrid models.

informal_sketch.intuition: The same logic as Theorem 1 applies: total demand must be less than available time. We just swap in the more accurate DBF formulas derived for the hybrid models.
steps: Select the appropriate DBF formula based on the task model (IUB, MP, or Clairvoyant)
Sum the DBFs for all tasks
Check against interval length t
key_insights: The framework is modular; as long as a safe DBF is provided for a model, the schedulability test remains the same.
